newsitem.title: USA: Army general dismissed from post - NYT.
newsitem.headline: Army general dismissed from post - NYT.

text.p: An Army general who may have had an "improper relationship" with the civilian nurse who cared for his critically ill wife has been relieved of his duties, the New York Times said in Friday's editions.
Brig. Gen. Stephen Xenakis was dismissed from command of all Army medical operations in the Southeast, the Times reported.
Xenakis, 48, had commanded the Dwight Eisenhower Army Medical Centre at Fort Gordon, Ga., since December 1995, and oversaw six other Army hospitals through the Southeast and Puerto Rico.
A spokeswoman for Xenakis said she could not reach him for comment Thursday night.
Army officials said he had been relieved of his post but declined to provide further information.

Unnamed sources from the military and Congress told the Times that the Army's inspector general opened an inquiry into the matter in January, when an anonymous letter was sent accusing Xenakis of misconduct.
The exact relationship he may have had with the nurse was not immediately clear. However, his car had been seen parked outside her home at all hours, day and night, the Times said.
